changes.before: Create a named native dialog with an opener and a Close button that submits a method=dialog form.
changes.after: Open a named dialog, then close it and return to the page.

before: dialog represents a dialog box. Merely adding open shows it nonmodally; showModal() opens it modally in the browser’s top layer.

A modal dialog makes the background inert while it is open. A details disclosure does not do that.

Here, inert means the background page cannot receive user clicks or keyboard focus while the modal is active. The person interacts with the dialog instead; it does not mean background scripts stop running.
Name the dialog with aria-labelledby pointing to its visible heading. Do not put tabindex on the dialog itself.

A button can request opening through a small event handler. ```html

Packing tip

 ``` This demonstration uses a local inline handler; larger apps can attach a listener from their script.

A form with method="dialog" closes its containing dialog rather than submitting a network request.
```html
<form method="dialog"><button>Close tip</button></form>
```
Provide a visible close control and a sensible initial focus target. Native modal dialogs normally support Escape cancellation; do not suppress it without a strong reason.
After closing, verify focus returns to the opener. Check opening, keyboard movement, Escape and the visible close control in a real browser; attributes alone do not prove that experience.
after: `<dialog>` is a box for a focused message or task. Calling its `showModal()` method opens it as a modal: the person uses the dialog before returning to the rest of the page.
While a modal is open, the background cannot receive clicks or keyboard focus. Adding the HTML attribute `open` only shows a nonmodal dialog; it does not block the background.
Give the dialog a visible heading. Use `aria-labelledby` to point to that heading’s id so assistive tools can announce the dialog’s name. Do not put tabindex on the dialog itself.

This button opens a small dialog. ```html

Packing tip

 ``` The text inside `onclick` is JavaScript. `document.getElementById('tip')` finds the dialog by id. `.showModal()` opens it. The dialog’s `aria-labelledby` points to its visible heading.

Put this form inside the dialog to close it.

```html
<form method="dialog">
  <button type="submit" autofocus>Close tip</button>
</form>
```

`method="dialog"` makes submission close the dialog instead of sending data. `autofocus` asks the browser to focus this button when the dialog opens.
Keep a visible close button so the way out is clear. A native modal also normally closes with Escape. After it closes, focus should return to the button that opened it.

On the starter opener, add an onclick handler that finds `research-dialog` and calls showModal(). Give the dialog `aria-labelledby="dialog-title"`. Add a method="dialog" form containing a button named exactly `Close`, with autofocus. Run the checks, then try opening, Escape, Close and focus returning to the opener.

before.question: You add open to dialog but never call showModal(). Does that alone make the background inert?
choices: Yes, every visible dialog is modal
No, open alone displays a nonmodal dialog
Only when the heading is h2
before.explanation: The modal behavior comes from showModal(), not merely the presence of open.

after.question: You add open to dialog without calling showModal(). Is the background blocked?
choices: Yes. Every visible dialog blocks the background.
No. Open alone shows a nonmodal dialog.
Only if the title uses h2.
after.explanation: `showModal()` starts modal behavior. The open attribute alone only makes the dialog visible.
